title: Revamp onboarding pipeline: automated metadata validation, pinning, and perf-profile publish
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Onboarding new open and vendor models currently requires several manual steps: metadata edits, fingerprinting, creating a pinned variant, running perf benchmarks and then publishing a performance profile. This is slow, error-prone, and causes inconsistent catalog entries (missing compatibility fields, mismatched quantization tags, outdated kernel hints).

Goal: Build a repeatable, auditable pipeline and small CLI that takes a model bundle or manifest and produces a validated catalog entry, auto-generates a pinned variant (following pinning policy), runs a constrained perf harness to generate canonical latency/throughput numbers, and publishes a signed performance profile and docs stub. The pipeline must emit human-review PRs for edge cases and support a fully automated path for low-risk models.
acceptance_criteria: Create an onboarding CLI command `redwood-catalog onboard` that accepts model manifest URL or local bundle and produces a Draft catalog JSON conforming to schema-v2
Implement metadata validator with clear error/warning levels; no draft can be published if 'error' validations fail
Automate fingerprint creation (model id, digest of weights, architecture fingerprint) and include fingerprint field in final metadata
Auto-generate a pinned variant following new pinning-policy (pin to exact build + quantization/profile) and attach 'pinned_by' and 'pin_timestamp' metadata
Run perf harness in CI (short-run benchmark: 50 warmup + 200 samples at 32/128 context lengths) and publish a signed performance_profile.json with latency P50/P95/P99 and throughput numbers
Create a PR against catalog repo with: catalog metadata file, performance_profile.json, docs stub (MD) linking to perf graphs and compatibility matrix
Docs stub should include recommended 'default_variant' and 'fallbacks' and be linked to model catalog page in console after merge
Provide audit log entries (who initiated vs who approved) and emit a Slack notification to #catalog-ops on publish
End-to-end test coverage that simulates onboarding a small quantized model and a large fp16 model in CI
Runbook for manual rollback and emergency unpin flow documented in the PR template
technical_notes: Schema target: catalog-schema-v2; new required fields: fingerprint, compatibility_matrix, default_variant, pin_info
Fingerprint algorithm: sha256 over canonicalized model manifest + weights manifest; store base64 digest
Perf harness container must expose metrics to Prometheus and produce JSON with P50/P95/P99; implement jib/runner for isolation
Pinning policy: pin only GA models and models from vetted vendors unless flagged with label 'allow-auto-pin'
If perf harness fails or variance > 10% between runs, create PR in 'needs-review' mode rather than auto-publish
Add lint step that normalizes tag sets (quantization: q4f/q8a; hw hints: a100/h100/cpu)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable automated pipeline for internal 'research' namespace models only; manual approval required for publish
Phase 2 (controlled): add a small set of vetted vendor models with auto-publish allowed; monitor SLI deltas for 2 weeks
Phase 3 (open): allow community model onboarding but require a two-person approval for first publish
Monitoring: dashboard with counts of onboarded models, failed validations, perf variance alerts, and average time-to-publish
Fallback: CLI provides `redwood-catalog unpin` to revert pin and re-open previous default_variant
